paper_id: Yang and Liu - 2010 - Quality of Trilateration Confidence-Based Iterative Localization
title: Quality of Trilateration: Confidence-Based Iterative Localization
motivation: Coal mine sensor network prototype failed because noisy distance estimation degrades trilateration quality in four aspects.
problem_framing: Quantify geometric relationship and ranging noise to evaluate trilateration quality beyond binary feasible/unfeasible.
key_insight: Different geometric forms of trilaterations provide different accuracy levels; QoT enables selecting best trilaterations and avoiding flip ambiguity.
method_signature: QoT metric measures trilateration quality; CIL scheme iteratively selects highest-confidence trilaterations with refinement.
evaluation_criteria: Localization accuracy (meter error), confidence values, error propagation speed across network hops.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: In coal mine prototype, straightforward multilateration-based localization turns out to be a failure.
evidence_for_taste: localization turns out to be a failure
error propagation needs to be carefully considered
thinking_moves: 从工程失败反推需要超越二元分类的连续质量度量
将置信度定义为 trilateration 质量和参考节点置信度的乘积
将置信度计算问题转化为 Bellman-Ford 最短路径问题
用位置 refinement 机制在动态过程中持续改进精度
cites_own_work: M. Li and Y. Liu, 'Underground Coal Mine Monitoring with Wireless Sensor Networks'
